clips.why: Thesis cold open: Opus 4.5 changed coding, Opus 5 'felt more like a liability', and 5.5 is blowing him away. It has no tight in-band cut: it only lands at 'may have hit it' (96s) or 'Absolutely' (113s).
Clear insight: Fable has no zero-data-retention option, so ZDR-bound companies can't use it, and Opus 5.5 will become the most popular coding model on that detail alone.
Story with a point: max effort levels make the model loop forever. His own thread ran 6.5 hours writing a markdown plan on max and got only halfway.

His own Skatebench: going from x-high to max takes ~300 to ~5000 tokens per question (10x the cost) for a 1% score bump, so 'don't use max on this model'. The numbers support a verbal point and aren't just read off a chart.

Explains a real quirk: models trained before compaction was reliable learned to fear their context limit; OpenAI trained it out, Anthropic less so. It can open on 'not without its quirks' or directly on 'paranoia around the context window'.
Grounded take: Opus 5.5 is smaller and dumber than Fable, and on longer jobs the odds of hitting a failure spike go up, so be realistic before replacing Fable.

also_ok.why: He reads out an employee's 'sorry about that model' tweet and argues Anthropic is letting staff post freely, which is a nice cultural shift. Works from the words, but leans on the on-screen tweet.

Point: the model is cheaper per token but uses about 4x the tokens of GPT-6 Astra, and '2x faster doesn't matter if you need 4x more tokens'. It is built on read-out benchmark numbers, so accept but don't insist.
Both max-effort segments as one continuous rant (story plus Skatebench numbers).

Value take: a day of real work (visualizer, a PR) cost ~1% of his weekly limit, and it beats a Codex sub for $200. The start at 1198 (the work list) and the start at 1233 ('I can't believe I'm saying this') both work.
Short verdict: Opus is the right default for most things, but reach for Fable on frontend and marketing pages.
Quotable framing: Anthropic are the pre-training kings and OpenAI the post-training kings, but Anthropic has caught up on post-training. It is short.

negatives.why: WorkOS sponsor read; has a genuinely funny aside ('configuring Okta is hell'), but it's an ad.
Subscribe plea ('less than half of y'all are subbed').

Parallel sponsor read with a live speed race ('going now... still going').
High-energy reaction to the Fishslop 3D demo ('look at the stingray', 'what the fuck'); pure on-screen reaction.
